analysis.evidence: וַאֲנִי sets the speaker apart at the start of the verse. הִנְנִי מֵקִים then resumes the first person and states what he undertakes to do: establish his covenant with the addressees and their descendants.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ, “and,” prefixes the independent first-person common singular pronoun אֲנִי, “I.”
analysis.sense: I, as for me (the speaker set apart)

analysis.evidence: In מֵקִים אֶת בְּרִיתִי, אֶת marks בְּרִיתִי (“my covenant”) as the direct object of מֵקִים (“establishing”). The possessive suffix makes the noun definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God says מֵקִים אֶת בְּרִיתִי, “I am establishing my covenant.” The phrases אִתְּכֶם and וְאֶת זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם identify Noah and his sons, together with their descendants, as covenant partners.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

draft.change: Explain the existing Gen.9.9 citation under the preposition’s sense with-dealings-between-two.
draft.definition: With, introducing the other party to a covenant.
draft.evidence: Gen.9.9 distinguishes the covenant being established, אֶת בְּרִיתִי, from its partners, אִתְּכֶם וְאֶת זַרְעֲכֶם, “with you and with your descendants.”

analysis.evidence: In מֵקִים אֶת בְּרִיתִי אִתְּכֶם, “I am establishing my covenant with you,” בְּרִיתִי is what God establishes. אִתְּכֶם identifies the people with whom he establishes it. The parallel וְאֶת זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם extends the same relationship to “your descendants after you.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition אֵת takes the form אִתְּ־ before the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם.
analysis.sense: Introduces the party with whom a covenant is established.

analysis.evidence: God establishes his covenant with Noah and his sons and with זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם, “your descendants after you.” The plural suffix refers to the addressees, and אַחֲרֵיכֶם identifies the generations that follow them.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine plural possessive suffix. The singular noun refers collectively to descendants.

analysis.evidence: In זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם, “your descendants after you,” the suffix refers to the same people as אִתְּכֶם, “with you.” The covenant extends to the generations that succeed them.
analysis.morphology: The preposition אַחֲרֵי takes the second-person masculine plural suffix כֶם, referring to the people addressed.
